note: A waiver is a CEILING, never a mute, and --prove-waiver fails the lane if it changes no outcome. This lane makes routing refuse what it used to commit silently (28.5) and lay a branch per sink (28.7, 28.8). A correct refusal can move a candidate out of `route` before `validate` ever judges it, which lowers the denominator, and a correct branch can put belts in front of checks that never saw them. Those movements are this lane's to repay: integration runs --no-waivers on the merged tree.

waivers.cause: rule 28.5 turns a silently committed direction mismatch into a named refusal, and rule 28.7 refuses a demand whose branch cannot be laid; both show up here before the router learns to share a trunk
a sink that used to be claimed by a binding with no belt behind it now reports its real shortfall until the branch is laid
